sa27:0.3: 33 (27). Going from One Thing to the Next
sa27:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa27:2.1: There was then a certain monk who came to visit the Buddha.
sa27:2.2: He bowed his head, withdrew to stand at one side, and said to the Buddha,
sa27:2.3: “The Bhagavān says ‘going from one thing to the next.’
sa27:2.4: How does one go from one thing to the next?”
sa27:3.2: “Good, good! Do you want now to know about going from one thing to the next?”
sa27:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa27:5.2: “[Listen closely!] Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa27:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa27:5.4: Monk, heading for disillusionment with form, becoming free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it is called going from one thing to the next.
sa27:5.5: It’s the same with feeling, conception, volition, and awareness … heading for disillusionment with awareness, becoming free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it is called going from one thing to the next.”
sa27:6.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he celebrated and rejoiced.
